input.question: Why am I allergic to cats and is their a way to get over my allergy?
input.ground_truth: Depending on the severity of your allergy you can consider [allergy shots/immunotherapy](_URL_0_). I would make an appointment with an allergy specialist as there are different levels of effectiveness depending on your specific case. I started them 3 months ago. Its a big time commitment 2x/week for ~6months and then 1x/month for 3-5 years (probably closer to 5 years).

messages.content: You are a helpful AI assistant.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why am I allergic to cats and is their a way to get over my allergy?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a tiny body guard inside you called your "immune system." Its job is to keep you safe from things that might hurt you, like germs.

But sometimes, your body gets confused. It thinks a cat’s fur or some tiny things from a cat are bad guys, even though they’re not really dangerous. So, when you are near a cat, your body tries to protect you by making you sneeze, have itchy eyes, or get a runny nose. That’s what we call an allergy.

Now, can you "get over" your cat allergy? Sometimes, as you grow up, your body might stop thinking cats are so scary, and you might not get as sick around them. But it can take a long time.

Doctors can also help in some ways. They might give you medicines that help with the sneezing and itching when you’re around cats. There are also special shots called "allergy shots" that can help your body get used to cat stuff, but you have to get them many times over a long time.

So, you can’t just wake up one day and not be allergic, but there are ways to help make being around cats a little easier!
